best_for: Web developers and admins on Mac or Windows who move files between FTP or SFTP servers and cloud buckets like S3 or Backblaze B2, and want one free app for all of them.

points.title: One app, many backends
points.text: Besides FTP, SFTP, WebDAV and SMB, it connects to Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage, Azure, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, OneDrive and SharePoint, Dropbox, Google Drive, Box, and Nextcloud or ownCloud.

points.title: Free, with a donation prompt
points.text: Cyberduck is free software under GPL-3.0. After installs and updates it asks for a donation; a gift of at least USD 10 gets a personal registration key that turns the prompt off on all your computers. You can also buy it from the Mac App Store or Windows Store.

points.title: Encrypt before it leaves
points.text: Cryptomator vaults are supported, so file names and contents are encrypted on your machine before upload. Handy when the storage provider is not someone you fully trust.

points.title: Edit in place
points.text: Open a remote file in your usual editor and Cyberduck uploads it again when you save, so small fixes on a server do not need a download and re-upload by hand.

points.title: No mounted drive
points.text: Cyberduck is a browser window, not a disk in Finder or File Explorer. Mounting remote storage as a drive is a separate product from the same company, Mountain Duck.

points.title: No Linux app, but a CLI
points.text: The graphical app is for Mac and Windows only. The `duck` command-line tool runs on Linux, macOS and Windows for scripted transfers.

points.title: What runs it
points.text: Windows needs Windows 10 64-bit or later, and the installer here installs for all users. The Mac download is a universal zip for macOS 10.13 or later. The Windows listing keeps 72 versions; macOS lists only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
